tutorial.title: Intro to Node.js
tutorial.descriptionContent: Dive into the world of NodeJS and NPM before using it with React and Express

lessons.title: NodeJS
lessons.interactiveContent:
Node, short for Node.js, is an open-source runtime for running JavaScript outside the browser.

Server-side applications using JavaScript run mostly on Node.

lessons.title: NodeJS 2 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
So far, we've used Node to execute JavaScript outside of the browser environment. Going forward, you'll also use it to run servers.

Node enables us to build fast, scalable, and efficient server-side applications using JavaScript.

lessons.title: Installing Node
lessons.interactiveContent:
Mimo enables you to spin up a project without having to handle installing Node.

If you want to use it locally, you can check your version. Type node -v in a terminal. v stands for version. This will show your version.

Make sure to pick node, followed by -v.

lessons.title: Node Packages
lessons.interactiveContent:
Node comes with the Node Package Manager (NPM), a tool that allows you to install, manage, and share libraries and dependencies easily.

Type npm install x to install the package called x.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by install, and finally x.

lessons.title: NPM
lessons.interactiveContent:
NPM manages the installation of packages from a repository of public Node packages known as the NPM registry.

Node installation includes NPM. To check its version, use the command npm -v.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by -v.
lessons.hardModeContent:
NPM manages packages from the public Node package repository called the NPM registry.

Node installation includes NPM. Both tools use -v to show their version.

Check the installed package manager version in the terminal.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by -v.

lessons.title: npm init
lessons.interactiveContent:
To create a project using Node we must initialize the project.

A project can be created using the command npm init in the terminal.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by init.

lessons.title: npm install
lessons.interactiveContent:
To install packages, type npm install or npm i followed by the package name.

For example, let's install x, a package that you may find useful.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by install, and finally x.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To install packages, use npm install or npm i followed by the package name.

Install x with the shorter form of the install command.

Make sure to pick npm, followed by i, and finally x.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent: Did you know? At Mimo, we handle package management for you. If you head to the projects section, you can install packages without NPM.

lessons.title: Question: NodeJS
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does Node extend the usability of JavaScript?

Node enables JavaScript to work outside of the browserNode adds more built-in functions to frontend JavaScript

Node enables JavaScript to work outside of the browser.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You run a JavaScript server with Node. You close your browser. What happens to the server?

It can keep running because Node runs JavaScript outside the browser.It stops because Node needs the browser to execute JavaScript.It keeps running only if another browser window is open.

It can keep running because Node runs JavaScript outside the browser.

lessons.title: Question: Installing Node
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the output of the terminal when you check for the installed Node version with node -v?

The version number, like v20.17.0A boolean that states whether Node is installed or not

The version number, like v20.17.0.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You run node -v before starting a project. What kind of result confirms the installed Node version?

A version string such as v20.17.0A boolean saying whether Node is installedA list of packages installed by NPM

A version string such as v20.17.0.

lessons.title: Question: NPM
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the NPM registry?

A repository where you can find packages to install for your projectsA framework that enables JavaScript to work on the backend

A repository where you can find packages to install for your projects.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need a library to add to a Node project. Where would NPM look for a public package to install?

The NPM registry, a repository of packages for projects.The Node runtime, which stores all project packages.An Express server, which publishes JavaScript libraries.

The NPM registry, a repository of packages for projects.

lessons.title: Question: npm init
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does npm init do?

It initializes a Node projectIt adds the requested NPM package to your project

It initializes a Node project.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You have an empty folder and want NPM to create its project setup. Which command should you run first?

npm initnpm installnode -v

Make sure to pick npm init.

lessons.title: Question: npm install
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the correct command to install an NPM package?

npm install xnpm init x

npm install x.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A project already has package.json. Which command installs the NPM package named x?

npm install xnpm init xnode x

Make sure to pick npm install x.
